source_en: Late close at my market stall. Fixed the freezer door.
Home after the late shift. Scrubbed the block, all clean.
Coming back to sharpen the cleavers.
Checking the seals on the back door.
Gauze ration from the polyclinic. Two rolls a week.
Bartering meat at the market. Protein is protein.
Back from the boundary fence. I just wanted to see the sky.
The stall is empty. Nothing left to cut. Going home.
Reentering the gates to find a place to sleep that isn't grey.
Home from my desk at the tax inspectorate. Day shift.
First time in the city. Looking for work at the market.
Sitting as a model for the art institute portrait class.
Vegetarian society meeting. I have not touched meat in years.
Collecting my pension after forty years at the bakery.
Fainted at the sight of blood again. Seeing the doctor.
Government inspector, checking radiation safety protocols.
Coming from a wedding. I was the flower boy.
Restocking my stall. Fresh deliveries every morning now.
Careful with the permit. My hands are always a bit... slick.
The bandages? Just a little accident at the shop. Don't stare.
I have a special cut of rib waiting for me inside.
The hunger... it isn't in my stomach anymore. It's in my teeth.
Do you hear the metal grinding, officer? It never truly stops.
I feel the air touching my raw face through the gauze.
Here, take my papers. Sorry got a little blood on them. Comes with the profession.
You look like you'd make a good filet mignon.
Hope you're not sick of seeing me. Cause I've been dying to see you.
Stop by later. I’ll give you a 'cut' of the profits. Get it?
Try to stay plump, officer. It’s a better look for you.
Go on. The world is just one big cold-storage anyway.
Solitary? Well, at least I won't have to share my lunch.
I’ll be practicing my knife skills on the wallpaper. Don't worry.
A box is a box. Eventually, we all get wrapped up.
Aw, and I was just starting to like your face.
A bit overkill, don't you think? I’m already half-mummified.
There it is... the big... silent... punchline.
Solitary confinement? My favorite kind of kitchen. Very private.
Oh good. I’ve been meaning to practice my patience.
The walls look very chewy. I'll let you know how they taste.
First clean cut I've ever been on the receiving end of...
Hm. Thought it would sting more. I’m almost... impressed.
There’s something almost poetic... about going out this cleanly...
Where are you coming from?
My stall at the end of the market row. Scrubbed the block, fixed the freezer door. Late shift, as always.
The polyclinic, for gauze. They ration it now, two rolls a week. Then the stall to check the seals on the back door.
Out by the boundary fence. I wanted to see the sky. The stall is empty. Nothing left to cut.
The meat plant on the river road. I run a line there, day shift. Good union job, regular hours.
The polyclinic. They finally took the stitches out. The grinder only got me last month, you know.
The burns ward. They say my face has healed nicely since the kitchen fire. Bandages come off soon.
Are you experiencing any symptoms?
My back, like every butcher's back. The face itches under the gauze. That is all, officer.
Sweating more than I should. I stand up fast and the room goes dark. And I am hungry. Always hungry.
My hands shake since last week. Bad trait for a man with knives. I still cut straight.
Nothing at all. Never had a sore back in my life. Twenty years lifting carcasses and not one twinge.
Healthy as a bull. The doctor says I have the blood pressure of a schoolboy. I barely eat these days.
Steady as ever, look. I sold the stall in the spring anyway. Have not touched a knife since.
Careful with the permit. My hands are always a bit slick.
You ever notice how much quieter the streets have gotten at night? I love that.
I have a special cut waiting back at the shop. Been looking forward to it all day.
Do you hear the grinding? It does not stop. I have stopped trying to make it stop.
People bring me all sorts of things to barter now. I accept most of it. Protein is protein.
The hunger has gotten very specific lately. Hard to explain over a booth.
You look like you have not slept, officer. Neither have I. I do not miss it.
The bandages are dry today. First time in a while. I have been testing a theory.
I am having a very productive week. All things considered.
